my-day.title: My day
my-day.summary: A university student walks through an ordinary Monday, from breakfast to bed. Times, days of the week and daily verbs.
translation: I am Tomoko Kawakami. I am a second-year university student, and I live in Tokyo. Today is Monday. I will tell you about my day.
Every morning I get up at half past six. Breakfast is a small piece of bread and an egg. I leave home at 7:40 and walk about ten minutes to the station. On the train I always read a book.
University starts at nine. In the morning I have Japanese and English classes. My Japanese teacher is a woman, and she is very kind. I eat lunch with my friends in the school cafeteria.

In the afternoon I study at the library for about three hours. I leave school at half past four and work part-time at a shop in front of the station. My part-time job is on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays.
I get home around nine. After I eat dinner, I phone my mother. My mother lives in Hokkaido. Every day is very busy, but it is fun. I go to bed around eleven.

rain-on-the-mountain.title: Rain on the mountain
rain-on-the-mountain.summary: Two friends set off early for a mountain walk, and the rain comes sooner than forecast. Directions, nature and the weather.
translation: Last Saturday I went to the mountains with my friend Ms. Oki. She works at my company, and she loves mountains.
We got up at five in the morning and took the six o'clock train. It was very quiet on the train. When I looked outside, the sky was white and a little dark.

At eight we arrived at the station at the foot of the mountain. From there the two of us walked up. There were many tall trees on both the right and the left of the path. The water in a small river was very clean.
Around eleven it started to rain. The forecast had said "rain from the afternoon", but it came a little early. We went into an old hut and rested.
In the hut, Ms. Oki gave me some hot tea. The two of us ate rice balls and listened to the sound of the rain. She said, "The mountains are nice in the rain too."
An hour later the rain stopped and the weather cleared up. We did not go all the way to the top, but it was a really fun day. Next month the two of us will go again.

first-weeks-in-japan.title: My first weeks in Japan
first-weeks-in-japan.summary: A student from Indonesia arrives in Japan, gets help at a busy station, and settles in. Travel, food and family.
translation: I am Rina. I come from Indonesia. Last month I started at a Japanese university. Now I live in a small apartment near the university.
The day I came to Japan, it was raining. I went from the airport to the university by train. There were a lot of people at the station, and I could not really understand the station names.
Then a man in a white shirt asked me, "Where are you going?" When I told him the name of my university, he rode the train with me.
Japanese food is delicious. Every day I buy a cheap boxed lunch at a shop near school. But I am still not very good with Japanese fish.
On weekends I walk around town with my friends. Last Sunday we went to a big park and took lots of photos near the pond.
Next summer my mother and father are coming to Japan. I want to show the two of them a Japanese town. Before then, I want to speak Japanese better.

the-school-cat.title: The school cat
the-school-cat.summary: A white cat visits a school every day, until one day she doesn't. Counting, places around a school and a surprise ending.
translation: At my school there is a white cat. Her name is Yuki. Yuki doesn't belong to anyone, but everyone at school knows her.
Every morning at about eight, Yuki comes to the front of the school gate. When the students say "Good morning", Yuki says "Meow" in a small voice.
During morning classes, Yuki often sleeps under a tree outside the classroom. On sunny days you can see white Yuki from the window. The teacher says, "Don't look outside, please read your book."
At lunch break, Yuki goes behind the gym. There, Mr. Tanaka gives her water and food every day. Mr. Tanaka teaches science, and he is sixty years old.
One rainy day, Yuki did not come to school. She did not come the next day either. Everyone was very worried.
Three days later, in the morning, Yuki was in front of the gate. But she was not alone. Behind her were four little kittens. Mr. Tanaka laughed and said, "From today there are five of you, then."

a-present-for-dad.title: A present for Dad
a-present-for-dad.summary: Two siblings shop for a Father's Day present on a small budget. Prices, directions and big numbers.
translation: Next Sunday is Father's Day. My younger brother and I went to buy a present for our father.
If you leave by the west exit of the station and walk south for about five minutes, there is a big department store. Inside, there are about a hundred shops.
On the first floor there was a watch shop. Our father's watch is old, so I thought a new watch would be good. But even the cheapest watch was 20,000 yen. Our money came to 6,000 yen altogether.

Next we went to the bookshop upstairs. Our father likes books about mountains. My brother said, "How about this?" and showed me a book with lots of photos of long rivers and high mountains. The book was 2,800 yen.
After buying the book, we also bought a white handkerchief for 1,000 yen. Then we went home without saying anything.
On Sunday morning we gave our father the presents. He looked at the book and said, "Next month, let's all go to this mountain." He looked very happy.

a-friend-from-abroad.title: A friend from abroad
a-friend-from-abroad.summary: A classmate from Canada talks about his country over dinner and makes an invitation. Countries, descriptions and plans.
translation: In my class there is a student who came from abroad. His name is Tom. Tom's country is Canada. This is his second year in Japan.
Tom is very tall and has long hair. His Japanese is good, too. Every day he writes a diary in Japanese.
Last Friday I had dinner with Tom at a restaurant near school. Tom asked, "Of all Japanese food, what do you like best?" I answered, "Tempura."
Tom told me a lot about Canada. Canada is a very big country, and he says the winters are long and cold. Near Tom's house there is a big river and some mountains.
Tom said, "Why don't you come to Canada next summer holiday? Please stay at my house." I have never been abroad.
Now I study English every day. Next year I want to speak English in Tom's country.

camping-by-the-river.title: Camping by the river
camping-by-the-river.summary: A family spends two days camping beside a river: playing in the water, a fire, and a sky full of stars. Family, nature and time.
translation: At the beginning of August, my family went camping near a river. There were four of us: my father, my mother, my older sister and me. It took three hours by car.
It was 1 p.m. when we arrived at the campsite. My father and I put up the tent. My mother and sister made lunch under a tree.
In the afternoon we played in the river. The water was very cold, but it felt good. There were lots of small fish. My sister took lots of photos of them.
In the evening we lit a fire outside and grilled meat and vegetables. My father said, "Please don't run near the fire." The dinner we all ate together was delicious.
After dinner we looked at the sky. Unlike the sky in town, we could see lots of stars. A big moon was out, too. My mother said, "When I came here ten years ago, the stars were beautiful then too."
The next morning it rained. We went home early, but it was a really fun two days.

the-new-ramen-shop.title: The new ramen shop
the-new-ramen-shop.summary: A long queue, a tiny ramen shop, and a meal too big to finish. Prices, counting and time.
translation: Last month a new ramen shop opened in front of the station. The shop is called Yamakawa. Every day there is a long queue outside it.
On Tuesday I had the day off work, so in the afternoon I tried going on my own. It was half past two, but there were still about ten people in front of the shop.
After waiting about thirty minutes, I went in. The shop was small, with only eight seats. It is run by a young man and his mother.
There were only three things on the menu. Regular ramen is 800 yen, large ramen is 1,000 yen, and gyoza are 500 yen. I had the large ramen and gyoza.
The ramen was delicious. But the large ramen was really big, and I could only eat half of the gyoza. The mother laughed and said, "Next time, please have the regular one."
Next week I am going with a friend. This time I will have the regular ramen.

my-town.title: My town
my-town.summary: A high-school student describes their small town: what lies to the north, south, east and west, and the summer festival. Directions and big numbers.
translation: My town is about two hours by train from Tokyo. It is a small town, with about 30,000 people.
To the north of the town there is a high mountain, and to the south there is a long river. The mountain is called Shiroyama. In winter, the top of the mountain turns white.
The station is on the west side of town. In front of the station there is an old bookshop, a small café and a bank. They say the bookshop has been there for a hundred years.
On the east side of town is the high school I go to every day. It has about 600 students. Behind the school there are about a thousand big trees, and in spring it is very beautiful.
Every July there is a big festival near the river. On that day, more people come from outside than live in the town. At night you can see fireworks, too.
It isn't a big city like Tokyo, but I love this town. Please come and visit.

school-on-a-day-off.title: School on a day off
school-on-a-day-off.summary: A student rushes to school, only to find the gate shut and one teacher inside. Days of the week and a small mix-up.
translation: This morning I got up at seven. I washed my face in a hurry and left home without eating breakfast. It was very quiet outside.
I took my usual train. But there was not a single student on it. There were not many office workers either. I thought, "Something is strange."
When I got to school, the gate was shut. There was nobody in the schoolyard, either. I waited in front of the gate for about ten minutes.
Then Mr. Yamaguchi came out of the school. He was wearing a white shirt and holding some flowers. He asked, "Good morning. Today is Sunday, you know. Why did you come to school?"
I was very embarrassed. Last night I had been reading a book until late, so I didn't know what day it was.
Mr. Yamaguchi laughed and said, "I came to water the school's flowers. Would you like to help?" I watered the flowers with him for about an hour, and then went home.
